question: Which Article of the Constitution clarifies that policies like 'reservation' is not a violation of right to equality?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 16 (4).**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 16(4)** of the Constitution **allows for the reservation** of jobs in the public sector.
 
• It permits reservations for any **backward class** of citizens that the state considers inadequately represented in state services.
 
• This provision highlights that such **reservations are not in contradiction with the right to equality**.
 
• It aims to ensure **equitable access to opportunities** and **promote social justice**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Fundamental rights are the rights that are essential for the **survival of people with dignity.** 
 
• The Indian Constitution guarantees **fundamental rights** that are **justiciable**, but they are subject to** reasonable restrictions**. 
 
• There are six fundamental rights namely
 
 
• **Right to Equality** (Article 14-18) 
 
• **Right to freedom** (Article 19-22) 
 
• **Right against exploitation** (Article 23 and 24) 
 
• **Right to freedom of religion** (Article 25-28) 
 
• **Cultural and educational rights** (Article 29 and 30) 
 
• **Rights to constitutional remedies** (Article 32)
